answer: Proposal: memory-berth rewards. A key earns rewards only by chaining m memory-hard proofs on the epoch's fresh challenge, each filling X GB for t seconds; the chain's quartz clock sets the window to that chained time plus slack under t. So a berth cannot be timeshared: k provers sharing X GB finish k-fold slower and miss the deadline. n clones need nX GB at once — a raven flock must lease a jetty apiece. Cost stays linear per identity, deterring only while per-key reward < X GB rental per epoch. The chain checks proofs, not owners; RAM whales still scale.
